title: Hearty Japanese Pork Gyoza
description: Garlicky, flaky dumplings filled with scallions and pork, perfect for a high‑protein festive meal.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine ground pork, shredded cabbage, chopped scallions, minced garlic, grated ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, and water, mixing until fully incorporated.
Cover the mixture and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Meanwhile, bring a pot of water to a rolling boil and blanch the shredded cabbage for 1 minute, then drain and set aside to cool.
Warm a nonstick skillet over medium heat and lightly oil it, then place a dumpling wrapper and spoon 1 tablespoon of filling into the center, leaving a small space at the edge.
Fold the wrapper in half, pinching the edges together to seal, and press down firmly with a spatula to create a crisp seal.
Repeat steps 4 and 5 with the remaining wrappers and filling, stacking the sealed gyoza on a clean surface.
Spray the skillet with a light mist of water and cover with a lid, allowing the gyoza to steam for 3 minutes until the wrappers are translucent.
Remove the lid, increase heat to medium-high, and let the gyoza fry for an additional 2 minutes until the bottoms are golden and crispy.
Transfer the finished gyoza to a plate and drizzle with a squeeze of fresh lemon or a dash of chili oil if desired.
Serve immediately hot, accompanied by a small bowl of dipping sauce made with soy sauce, rice vinegar, and a hint of sesame oil.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F and let it rest for 3 minutes before serving.
